extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners/attorneys before the USPTO, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order implementing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 that excludes a practitioner from practice before the USPTO, describes notice/response procedures, publication and service requirements, account suspensions, compliance duties, and the process/conditions for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the United States Patent and Trademark Office for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complaint requests imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the state court order. The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline unless one or more of the reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1) are shown to exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and response procedure (service and response window)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' was sent by certified mail notifying Respondent and provided an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Notice and Order cannot be delivered, it may be published in the Official Gazette. Failure to file a timely response may permit the USPTO to determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, the Office determined there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and that exclusion from practice is the appropriate discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A lack of opposing response supports a determination that reciprocal discipline identical to the state-imposed discipline is appropriate absent showings under § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided template (including respondent's name, registration number, basis for discipline, and citation to the underlying state order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice should state the respondent's name, registration number, that the order concerns exclusion from practice for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), and reference the state disciplinary action (e.g., State of Oklahoma ex rel. Oklahoma Bar Association v. Jason David Smith, SCBD No. 7326 (Jul. 26, 2023)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public under § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be provided to the relevant enforcement agencies and courts; the publication and notice obligations are part of the disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order does not restate § 11.58; practitioners should consult § 11.58 for specific duties (e.g., client notification, transfer of files, refunding unearned fees) required upon discipline/exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization to disable or suspend USPTO.gov accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO is authorized to disable or suspend any USPTO.gov accounts registered to Respondent as of the date of the Final Order (including, but not limited to, all accounts that Respondent has ever established, sponsored, or used in connection with any patent, trademark, or other matter before the USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may act to disable or suspend accounts without further action beyond the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for or obtaining USPTO verified Electronic System accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO verified Electronic System account, shall not obtain a USPTO verified Electronic System account, nor shall he have his name added to a USPTO verified Electronic System account, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition is ongoing until reinstatement under the procedures of 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using, assisting, or accessing USPTO systems for filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is prohibited from using, assisting others in using, or accessing any USPTO.gov account(s) or other USPTO filing systems for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, until reinstatement, Respondent is prohibited from (1) opening or activating any USPTO.gov account(s) to be used for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO; (2) applying for or attempting to apply for any USPTO.gov account(s) to be used for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO; (3) verifying or attempting to verify any other person's credentials in connection with USPTO.gov account(s) to be used for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO; and (4) sponsoring or attempting to sponsor USPTO.gov account(s) to be used for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure and responsibility to seek re-activation (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Until a petition seeking Respondent's reinstatement to practice before the USPTO is granted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the prohibitions and disallowances remain in effect. Nothing obligates the USPTO to re-activate disabled or suspended accounts sua sponte; it is Respondent's sole responsibility to initiate any re-activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires filing the petition and meeting the standards of § 11.60; account reactivation is not automatic and must be requested by the respondent upon successful reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of discipline: underlying state ethical violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court of the State of Oklahoma approved Respondent's resignation from the practice of law based on ethical grounds; Respondent resigned without contesting specific allegations that his conduct involved 13 violations of Rules 1.1, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.15, 8.4(a), (c) and (d) of the Oklahoma Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline at the USPTO is predicated on the state-imposed discipline and the specific ethical rule violations alleged in the underlying state proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service/certificate of service requirements for disciplinary orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order was sent to Respondent by certified mail (receipt nos. listed), first-class mail, and to addresses provided to the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a); and to an address and email where the OED Director reasonably believes Respondent receives mail and electronic correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service methods include certified mail, first-class mail, and email to addresses reasonably believed to be used by the respondent, consistent with § 11.11(a).
